Sequences and partial sums（数列与部分和）

A sequence lists terms in order. A series adds terms. Substitute the required positive integer into the nth-term rule. If a partial sum is given, recover a term by subtracting successive partial sums.（数列与求和分开。）
T<sub>n</sub> = S<sub>n</sub> − S<sub>n−1</sub> for n ≥ 2; T<sub>1</sub> = S<sub>1</sub>.
Given S<sub>n</sub> = 3n<sup>2</sup> + n, find T<sub>2</sub> and T<sub>n</sub>.

S<sub>2</sub> = 3(4)+2 = 14 and S<sub>1</sub> = 4. Hence T<sub>2</sub> = 14−4 = 10. Expand S<sub>n−1</sub> = 3(n−1)<sup>2</sup>+(n−1) = 3n<sup>2</sup>−5n+2. Subtract to obtain T<sub>n</sub> = 6n−2. Check n=2 to get 10.
Do not confuse a term T<sub>n</sub> with its cumulative sum S<sub>n</sub>.
Arithmetic progressions（等差数列）
An arithmetic progression has a constant difference d. Start with a and add d exactly n−1 times to reach term n. Pair the first and last terms to understand the sum formula.
Tn = a+(n−1)d; Sn = n2[2a+(n−1)d].
For 5, 8, 11, …, find the tenth term and the sum of ten terms.
a=5 and d=3. T10=5+9(3)=32. S10=102(5+32)=5(37)=185. There are nine gaps between ten terms.
Use n−1 gaps, not n gaps.
Geometric progressions（等比数列）
A geometric progression multiplies each term by the same ratio r. Divide a term by the preceding nonzero term to identify r. The finite sum exists for negative ratios too.
Tn = arn−1; Sn = a(1−rn)1−r for r ≠ 1; if r=1, Sn=na.
For 3, 6, 12, …, find T<sub>5</sub> and S<sub>5</sub>.
Check the sign of r and keep the numerator and denominator in matching order.
Infinite geometric series（无穷等比级数）
An infinite sum approaches a finite limit only when the magnitudes of successive terms shrink. This requires the absolute value of the ratio to be less than one.
S∞ = a1−r when |r| < 1.
Find the infinite sum 12+6+3+….
a=12 and r=0.5. Since |0.5| < 1, the sum converges. S<sub>∞</sub>=12÷(1−0.5)=24. For comparison, the first three terms sum to 21, below the limiting value.
For |r| ≥ 1, do not apply the infinite-sum formula.
Interest and periodic rates（利息与每期利率）
Simple interest uses the original principal throughout. Compound interest earns interest on the accumulated balance. Match the rate period to the number of periods.
A=P(1+rt) for simple interest; A=P(1+i)n for compound interest; i=rm, n=mt.
Invest $1000 at a nominal 6% per year, compounded monthly, for two years.
Write r=0.06, m=12, i=0.005, n=24. A=1000(1.005)<sup>24</sup>≈$1127.16. Interest earned is A−1000≈$127.16. Retain calculator precision until the final cent.
A nominal annual rate is not a monthly rate.
Future value of an annuity（年金终值）
For equal end-of-period deposits, the first deposit earns interest for n−1 periods and the final deposit earns none. Adding these balances gives a geometric series.
FV=R(1+i)n−1i; an annuity due multiplies this value by (1+i).
Deposit $100 at the end of each month for one year at 1% monthly interest.
R=100, i=0.01, n=12. FV=100[(1.01)<sup>12</sup>−1]÷0.01≈$1268.25. Total deposits are $1200, so interest is about $68.25.
Decide whether deposits occur at the beginning or end before choosing the formula.
Present value and discounting（现值与贴现）
Present value reverses compound growth. A future payment is worth less today when the discount rate is positive. A stream of equal end-of-period payments is an ordinary annuity.
PV=FV(1+i)n; PVannuity=R1−(1+i)−ni.
Find the present value of five annual $1000 receipts at 5% per year.
Use R=1000, i=0.05, n=5. PV=1000[1−(1.05)<sup>−5</sup>]÷0.05≈$4329.48. Five undiscounted payments total $5000, so the smaller result is reasonable.
Do not use the future-value formula for a value at time zero.
Comparing financial offers（比较金融方案）
Use the same valuation date and rate period when comparing alternatives. The effective annual rate includes compounding within a year.
Effective annual rate = (1+rm)m−1.
Compare a nominal 6% compounded monthly with 6% compounded annually.
Monthly compounding gives (1+0.06÷12)<sup>12</sup>−1≈0.061678=6.1678%. Annual compounding gives 6%. Thus monthly compounding earns more on an investment, and costs more on a comparable debt.
Compare effective rates, not just quoted nominal percentages.
Sets and complements（集合与补集）
A union contains outcomes in either set. An intersection contains outcomes in both. A complement is always relative to the stated universal set.
n(A∪B)=n(A)+n(B)−n(A∩B).
In a group of 30, 18 study A, 15 study B, and 8 study both. How many study neither?
The union contains 18+15−8=25 people. Neither contains 30−25=5. The subtraction removes the duplicate counting of the eight people in both sets.
Do not subtract the intersection twice.
Counting choices（计数原理）
Multiply counts for successive choices when every earlier choice has the stated number of later choices. Add counts for disjoint alternatives.
For independent stages with a and b choices, total choices = ab.
How many outfits can be formed from 3 shirts and 2 trousers?
Choose a shirt in 3 ways. Each shirt can be paired with either of 2 trousers. Total=3×2=6. List the six pairs as a check.
For alternatives that overlap, remove the overlap before adding.
Permutations（排列）
Order matters in an arrangement. Choosing the first position leaves one fewer choice for the next position when repetition is forbidden.
P(n,r)=n!(n−r)!; repeated identical items give n!n1!n2!⋯.
Choose a president and secretary from 5 people, with no person holding both posts.
The president has 5 choices. For each, the secretary has 4. Total=5×4=20=P(5,2). A and B swapping roles produces a different result.
Do not use combinations when roles or order differ.
Combinations（组合）
A combination selects an unordered group. Divide the permutation count by the r! orders of the selected people.
C(n,r)=n!r!(n−r)!.
Select a committee of 2 from 5 people.
P(5,2)=20 ordered selections. Every pair is counted 2!=2 times. C(5,2)=20÷2=10.
State whether repetition is allowed before calculating.
Equally likely outcomes（等可能概率）
The counting formula applies when all elementary outcomes are equally likely. Specify the sample space before counting favourable outcomes.
P(A)=n(A)n(S); P(A′)=1−P(A).
Roll one fair die. Find the probability of an even result.
S={1,2,3,4,5,6}. A={2,4,6}. There are 3 favourable outcomes out of 6. P(A)=3÷6=0.5.
Do not assume unequal outcomes have equal probabilities.
Probability using combinations（用组合求概率）
For a sample drawn without replacement, count unordered selections in the numerator and denominator when order is irrelevant.
P(A)=favourable selectionsall equally likely selections.
A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. Draw 2 without replacement. Find the probability both are red.
All pairs=C(5,2)=10. Red pairs=C(3,2)=3. Therefore P=3÷10=0.3. Sequentially, (3÷5)(2÷4)=0.3 as a check.
Without replacement, the second denominator decreases.
Union and intersection（并集与交集概率）
Inclusive or allows both events to occur. Mutually exclusive events cannot occur together, but independent events can.
P(A∪B)=P(A)+P(B)−P(A∩B).
Given P(A)=0.4, P(B)=0.5 and P(A∩B)=0.2, find P(A∪B) and P(neither).
Mutually exclusive and independent are different conditions.
Tree diagrams（树状图）
Multiply probabilities along a branch. Add disjoint complete branches that meet the event description. Branch probabilities leaving any node must total one.
P(A∩B)=P(A)P(B|A).
A bag has 3 red and 2 blue balls. Draw 2 without replacement. Find exactly one red.
Red then blue has probability (3÷5)(2÷4)=0.3. Blue then red has probability (2÷5)(3÷4)=0.3. These paths are disjoint, so total=0.6.
Include both orders when the event is exactly one red.
Conditional probability（条件概率）
Conditioning restricts the sample space to the given event. Independence means this restriction does not change the probability of the other event.
P(A|B)=P(A∩B)P(B) for P(B)>0.
A group has 20 students, 12 taking A, 10 taking B and 6 taking both. Find P(A|B).
There are 10 B students, of whom 6 take A. P(A|B)=6÷10=0.6. Also P(A)=12÷20=0.6, consistent here with independence.
The denominator is the probability of the given event, not automatically P(A).
Probability review（概率复习）
Translate the event wording before selecting a formula. For at least one, a complement is often shorter than listing all cases.
P(at least one success)=1−P(no successes).
An independent trial succeeds with probability 0.2. Find at least one success in 3 trials.
P(no successes)=0.8<sup>3</sup>=0.512. Subtract from 1 to get 0.488.
The simple product requires independence.
Types of data（数据类型）

Categorical data describe categories. Numerical data describe counts or measurements. Counts are discrete; measurements are usually treated as continuous. Choose summaries appropriate to the variable.
Mode: most frequent value. Median: middle ordered value. Mean: Σxn.
Classify transport type, number of siblings and measured height.
Transport type is categorical nominal. Number of siblings is numerical discrete. Height is numerical continuous. A mean of transport category codes has no meaningful interpretation.
Numerical labels do not make a categorical variable quantitative.
Frequency distributions（频数分布）
A frequency table counts observations. Cumulative frequency tracks how many observations lie at or below successive ordered values. For grouped means, use class midpoints as estimates.
Mean = ΣfxΣf.
Values 1,2,3 have frequencies 2,3,1. Find the mean and median.
Total frequency=6. Weighted sum=1(2)+2(3)+3(1)=11. Mean=11÷6≈1.833. The ordered data are 1,1,2,2,2,3; the middle two are both 2, so median=2 and mode=2.
A grouped-data mean is generally an estimate, not an exact raw-data mean.
Variance and standard deviation（方差与标准差）
Variance measures squared distance from the mean. Standard deviation restores the original units. Choose population or sample notation according to the question.
σ2=Σ(x−μ)2N; s2=Σ(x−x̄)2n−1.
For the population 2,4,6, find its standard deviation.
μ=4. Squared deviations are 4,0,4. Population variance=8÷3. Population standard deviation=√(8÷3)≈1.633. Treating these data as a sample instead gives s=√(8÷2)=2.
The population and sample divisors are different.
Quartiles and transformations（四分位数与变换）
Interquartile range describes the spread of the middle half. Use the quartile convention required by the course or calculator. Adding a constant moves location without changing spread.
IQR=Q<sub>3</sub>−Q<sub>1</sub>; SD(aX+b)=|a|SD(X).
A variable has mean 10 and SD 3. Let Y=2X+5. Find its mean and SD.
E(Y)=2(10)+5=25. SD(Y)=|2|(3)=6. Variance(Y)=6<sup>2</sup>=36. Adding 5 changes the mean but not the SD.
Do not add a shift constant to standard deviation.
Correlation（相关）
A scatterplot shows direction, form and strength of association. Pearson correlation describes linear association. An outlier can strongly affect the fitted result.
If r=−0.9, describe the association and assess a causal claim.
The data show a strong negative linear association: larger x tends to accompany smaller y. The value alone does not prove that changing x causes y to change. Inspect the scatterplot and study design.
Correlation does not establish causation; r near zero does not rule out a nonlinear relationship.
Least-squares regression（最小二乘回归）
A regression line predicts y from x. The line passes through the pair of sample means. Predictions far beyond the observed x values are extrapolations.
ŷ=a+bx; b=rsysx; a=ȳ−bx̄.
Given x̄=10, ȳ=30, s<sub>x</sub>=2, s<sub>y</sub>=4 and r=0.8, find the regression line and predict at x=12.
The regression of x on y is generally not obtained by reversing the fitted y-on-x equation.
Discrete distributions（离散型分布）
A probability distribution assigns a nonnegative probability to each possible value, with total one. Expected value is a long-run weighted average and need not be a possible single outcome.
E(X)=Σxp(x); Var(X)=Σx<sup>2</sup>p(x)−[E(X)]<sup>2</sup>.
X takes 0,1,2 with probabilities 0.2,0.5,0.3. Find mean and variance.
Do not square probabilities when calculating E(X<sup>2</sup>).
Expected profit（期望利润）
Distinguish a gross payout from net profit after paying a fee. A fixed fee changes expected profit but not its variance.
E(aX+b)=aE(X)+b; Var(aX+b)=a<sup>2</sup>Var(X).
Using the previous distribution as dollar payouts, charge a $1 fee. Find expected net profit for the player.
Let Y=X−1. E(Y)=1.1−1=$0.10. Var(Y)=Var(X)=0.49. A fair fee for zero expected net profit would be $1.10.
State whose profit is being calculated: player and organiser have opposite signs.
Binomial model（二项分布）
A binomial variable counts successes in a fixed number of independent trials with the same success probability. Check these assumptions before using the formula.
P(X=k)=C(n,k)p<sup>k</sup>(1−p)<sup>n−k</sup>; E(X)=np; Var(X)=np(1−p).
Let X be binomial with n=5 and p=0.2. Find P(X=2).
Sampling without replacement from a small finite population usually violates constant p and independence.
Cumulative binomial events（二项累积事件）
Convert words such as at most, fewer than and at least into integer inequalities. Use a complement when it reduces calculation.
For the same X, find at least one success and at most one success.
At least one includes one; more than one does not.
Density and cumulative probability（密度与累积概率）
A continuous variable has probability equal to area under its density. The density may exceed one; only the total area must equal one. The probability at a single point is zero.
P(a≤X≤b)=∫<sub>a</sub><sup>b</sup>f(x) dx; F(x)=P(X≤x).
Let f(x)=kx on 0≤x≤2 and zero elsewhere. Find k and P(1≤X≤2).
Normalise: ∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>kx dx=2k=1, so k=0.5. The required area is ∫<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup>0.5x dx=[x<sup>2</sup>÷4]<sub>1</sub><sup>2</sup>=0.75.
A density value f(x) is not the point probability P(X=x).
Mean, variance and median（均值、方差与中位数）
Use weighted integrals instead of sums for a continuous distribution. The median divides the total area into equal halves.
E(X)=∫xf(x) dx; Var(X)=∫x<sup>2</sup>f(x) dx−[E(X)]<sup>2</sup>; F(m)=0.5.
For f(x)=0.5x on [0,2], find mean, variance and median.

E(X)=∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>0.5x<sup>2</sup> dx=4÷3. E(X<sup>2</sup>)=∫<sub>0</sub><sup>2</sup>0.5x<sup>3</sup> dx=2. Var(X)=2−16÷9=2÷9. Since F(x)=x<sup>2</sup>÷4 inside the interval, m<sup>2</sup>÷4=0.5, so m=√2.
Use the positive root for a median lying in [0,2].
Normal standardisation（正态标准化）
A normal model is symmetric about its mean. Standardisation measures distance from the mean in standard-deviation units. Keep track of whether the second parameter represents variance or SD.
Z=X−μσ; Z has standard normal distribution.
Let X be normal with mean 100 and SD 15. Find P(85≤X≤115).
Standardise both bounds: (85−100)÷15=−1 and (115−100)÷15=1. The standard normal area between −1 and 1 is approximately 0.6827.
Divide by SD σ, not by variance σ<sup>2</sup>.
Percentiles and inverse normal（百分位数与反求）
A percentile specifies cumulative area to the left. Use symmetry or a complement if your course table reports a different area convention.
x=μ+zσ.
Find the 90th percentile for the previous normal model.
Left-tail probability 0.9 corresponds to z≈1.2816. Therefore x=100+1.2816(15)≈119.22. Check that a 90th percentile lies above the mean.
For an upper-tail probability of 0.1, the left-tail area is 0.9, not 0.1.
Selecting a model（选择模型）
Start with the question type and assumptions. Fixed independent success trials suggest binomial; continuous bell-shaped measurements suggest normal; fixed repeated payments suggest an annuity.
Binomial: E(X)=np. Finance: match i and n to the same period.
A factory tests 10 independent items, each defective with probability 0.1. Find the probability none is defective.
Define X as the number defective. X is binomial with n=10, p=0.1. P(X=0)=0.9<sup>10</sup>≈0.34868. The definition of success is defectiveness here.
Define the counted event before assigning p.
Exam response and verification（考试作答与复核）
Write the model, substituted values, calculation and interpretation. State assumptions and units. Verify bounds, signs and numerical plausibility before rounding.
A probability must lie in [0,1]; variance must be nonnegative.
A response gives a probability of 1.2 and variance −0.4. Can either be accepted?

Neither is valid. Recheck whether the number 1.2 is actually a density rather than a probability. Recheck E(X<sup>2</sup>)−[E(X)]<sup>2</sup> for the variance and use full precision. Then state the corrected interpretation.
Do not round intermediate values before subtracting close quantities.
